slides.text: Series 1: MOHANDAS — December 1920
slides.visualDescription: "MOHANDAS" title card. Series subtitle: "The First Visit, 1920". Dramatic serif typography on black.

slides.text: The Land of 36 Forts
slides.visualDescription: Episode title card: "Episode 1 — The Land of 36 Forts" over silhouette of ancient fort ruins at dawn.

slides.text: Johar Gandhi is The Reminiscence Book of Record of the Freedom Fighters of the Diversity Land of Erstwhile Central Province of British India
slides.visualDescription: Aerial view of dense Sal forests stretching to horizon, rivers cutting through. Ink illustration style.

slides.text: Chhattisgarh was a part of the Central Provinces.
slides.visualDescription: Map of undivided Central Provinces with Chhattisgarh region highlighted in warm ink wash.

slides.text: Chhattisgarh is named after the forts located here.
slides.visualDescription: Panorama of 36 ancient forts scattered across hills and forests — stylized, dramatic skyline.

slides.text: the two visits of Mahatma Gandhi in Chhattisgarh
slides.visualDescription: Village scene — mud huts, paddy fields, tribal families gathered around evening fire.

slides.text: Gandhi had a very wide influence in the state of Chhattisgarh, he had visited this province only twice
slides.visualDescription: Silhouette of Gandhi (from behind) standing at a railway platform, small figure against vast landscape.

slides.text: but without being here physically and without any direct communication, his ideology was widely spread to the far-flung areas of this state
slides.visualDescription: Ripple effect — a single stone dropped into still water, waves spreading outward. Visual metaphor.

slides.text: The untold stories of the freedom struggles in Chhattisgarh recorded on the pages of history have never been discussed in any meaningful way
slides.visualDescription: Ink drawing of freedom fighters walking on dusty road, some in chains, some carrying flags.

slides.text: Chhattisgarh gave strength and unconditional support to Mahatma Gandhi for the successful Indian freedom movement
slides.visualDescription: Hands of different skin tones and castes clasped together, breaking free from chains. Visual metaphor.

slides.text: Many areas of Chhattisgarh have now been merged in other states of India, and many families who could be the witness of freedom fighters migrated to Pakistan after the partition in 1947
slides.visualDescription: Families leaving homes — bundles on heads, walking away from ancestral land. Partition imagery.

slides.text: There is no information about many of the agitators who were involved in the Indian freedom movement from Chhattisgarh
slides.visualDescription: Empty courtyard of an old house, dust-covered photographs on wall, cobwebs.

slides.text: To write this book, I have been trying to find the relatives of Satyagrahis for about two-three years
slides.visualDescription: Author (Amir Hashmi) walking through village lanes, notebook in hand, asking elderly people.

slides.text: Their last descendants have ended in many families, some have left the state
slides.visualDescription: Old family tree drawn in ink, branches fading into smoke at the edges.

slides.text: the heroic saga of their ancestors is not known as a result of the race of life, poverty, illiteracy, and efforts to erase history
slides.visualDescription: A candle burning on a stack of old papers and books. Light against darkness. Visual metaphor.

slides.text: A person is best known for his Truth and Non-Violence
slides.visualDescription: Young Gandhi in South Africa — suited, determined expression, walking on a road alone.

slides.text: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was an eminent independence activist and an influential political leader who played a major role in India's struggle for independence
slides.visualDescription: Portrait of Gandhi — round glasses, gentle eyes, iconic profile. Dramatic rim lighting.

slides.text: Gandhi is known by different names, such as Mahatma (a great soul), Bapu (father in the Gujarati language), and father of the nation
slides.visualDescription: Collage of names in different scripts — Mahatma, Bapu, Father of the Nation — orbiting Gandhi's silhouette.

slides.text: In South Africa, Gandhi felt racial discrimination towards blacks and Indians. He faced humiliation on several occasions
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi being thrown off a train in South Africa. Dramatic angle, sense of injustice.

slides.text: he decided to fight racial discrimination... succeeded in establishing an organization called Indian National Congress in the year 1894
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi standing at podium with "Indian National Congress" banner in South Africa, crowd below.

slides.text: He returned to India in the year 1915 after living in South Africa for 21 years
slides.visualDescription: Ship on ocean, Gandhi at the bow looking toward India. Sunrise on the horizon. Visual metaphor: homecoming.

slides.text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, a senior leader of the Indian National Congress, invited Gandhi to join India's struggle for independence against British rule
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi meeting Gopal Krishna Gokhale — two men shaking hands, mutual respect.

slides.text: In the year 1915, Gandhi came to India and toured the villages of the country to prepare the strategy for the freedom struggle
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi walking barefoot through Indian villages, dusty roads, children following.

slides.text: Gandhi said that Satyagraha was like a banyan tree that has innumerable branches
slides.visualDescription: A banyan tree with massive roots — visual metaphor for Satyagraha.

slides.text: Gandhi gave the name of Satyagraha to his entire non-violent method of work. Satyagraha for him meant the exercise of pure self-force against all kinds of injustice, tyranny, and exploitation
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi's spinning wheel (charkha) in close-up, thread being drawn — symbolizing self-reliance.

slides.text: Gandhi said that Satyagraha can be adopted by anyone
slides.visualDescription: Split panel: Left — soldiers with weapons. Right — unarmed people standing firm.

slides.text: The great scientist Albert Einstein said of Gandhi that Future generations will find it difficult to believe that such a man made of flesh and blood ever came to earth
slides.visualDescription: Einstein writing at desk, looking up with wonder. Quote floating beside him.

slides.text: Mahatma Gandhi inspired the world's great moral and political leaders such as Martin Luther King Jr., Nelson Mandela, and the Dalai Lama
slides.visualDescription: World map with lines connecting India to South Africa, USA, Myanmar — showing Gandhi's global influence.

slides.text: He often wore only a loincloth and shawl
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi in loincloth and shawl, walking with his stick. Full-figure portrait, powerful simplicity.

slides.text: Mahatma Gandhi in Chhattisgarh
slides.visualDescription: Title card: "Mahatma Gandhi in Chhattisgarh" in dramatic typography over forest landscape.

slides.text: Mahatma Gandhi is an indelible name, despite only two visits to Chhattisgarh
slides.visualDescription: Map zooming into Chhattisgarh within India. The region glows as if awakening.

slides.text: Chhattisgarh played an important role under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi in the campaigns being run against the slavery of the British in India
slides.visualDescription: Chhattisgarh landscape with Congress flag being raised in a village square.

slides.text: Gandhi infused a political, social, and economic consciousness within the entire state, the region of Chhattisgarh was not untouched by his efforts
slides.visualDescription: A flame spreading from a single lamp to hundreds — visual metaphor for ideological spread.

slides.text: Leaders like Madhavrao Sapre, Vamanrao Lakhe started anti-British awakening in their respective areas
slides.visualDescription: Portrait of Madhavrao Sapre at a printing press, first issue of "Chhattisgarh Mitra".

slides.text: Pt. Sundarlal Sharma was active in the untouchable salvation program
slides.visualDescription: Pt. Sundarlal Sharma entering a temple with people of all castes. Dramatic doorway light.

slides.text: After the death of Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1920, Mahatma Gandhi emerged as the biggest leader of the Congress party
slides.visualDescription: Portrait of Lokmanya Tilak, somber, with funeral pyre in background fading.

slides.text: farmers in the Dhamtari region of Chhattisgarh protested against the tax imposed on the canal water of the British
slides.visualDescription: Farmers of Dhamtari region standing in flooded paddy field, canal water flowing. British officer pointing.

slides.text: Babu Chhotelal Srivastava had started the Kandel Satyagraha
slides.visualDescription: Babu Chhotelal Srivastava standing firm before a group of farmers, fist raised.

slides.text: Pt. Sundarlal Sharma went to Calcutta because Gandhi was about to come from Calcutta to Nagpur
slides.visualDescription: Pt. Sundarlal Sharma boarding a train, determination on face. Destination: Calcutta.

slides.text: Pt. Sharma informed Gandhi about the Kandel Satyagraha and accompanied him to Raipur
slides.visualDescription: Sharma speaking to Gandhi in a train compartment. Two figures, intimate conversation.

slides.text: By this time Gandhi's personality had already had an impact on the British
slides.visualDescription: British official reading a telegram — face turning pale. "Gandhi is coming." Visual tension.

slides.text: In 1917, in the same way, indigo farmers had agitated in Champaran
slides.visualDescription: Split scene: Champaran (indigo fields) on left, Kandel (canal/paddy) on right. Same pattern of resistance.

slides.text: The British accepted the demands of Kandel Satyagrahis even before Mahatma Gandhi reached Raipur
slides.visualDescription: British officers hastily signing documents, withdrawing orders. Sweat on brows.

slides.text: Thus Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi had his first stay in Chhattisgarh
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi stepping off train at Raipur platform. Crowd's POV — only his sandals visible at first.

slides.text: After the Civil Disobedience Movement, Gandhi had made a complete agreement with Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi and Dr. Ambedkar shaking hands. Solemn agreement.

slides.text: Mahatma Gandhi promised Dr. Ambedkar that he would make efforts throughout his life to eliminate the problem of untouchability in society
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi making a vow — one hand raised, one on heart. Light beam from above. Visual metaphor.

slides.text: Sevagram near Wardha, the residence of Mahatma Gandhi on the Nagpur-Mumbai rail route, had become a battlefield of truth and non-violence
slides.visualDescription: Sevagram ashram near Wardha — simple huts, spinning wheels, a battlefield of ideas.

slides.text: He reached Durg on 22 November, made Raipur his center, and took several meetings till 27 November at Dhamtari, Nawapara Rajim, Balodabazar, and Bilaspur
slides.visualDescription: Map showing Gandhi's 1933 route through Chhattisgarh — Durg, Raipur, Dhamtari, Bilaspur, marked with dots.

slides.text: In every meeting, he called upon the people of every class to free them from the disgusting problem of untouchability from society
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi speaking to a mixed crowd — people of all castes sitting together. Some touching his feet.

slides.text: Wherever Gandhi went to see him, thousands of people gathered to see him, people were eager to see him, hear him and touch his feet
slides.visualDescription: Massive crowd, overhead view — thousands gathered, a sea of humanity. Gandhi tiny at center.

slides.text: He got the Harijans entered the temple of Jayatu Sav Math located in the old township of Raipur
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi entering the Jaitusav Math temple with Harijan families. Temple doors opening wide. Visual metaphor: barriers falling.

slides.text: inaugurated an indigenous fair at Moti Bagh in Raipur, in which a crowd of one lakh people had gathered to see Gandhi
slides.visualDescription: Moti Bagh fairground — one lakh people, flags, stalls, energy. Gandhi at center like a sun with rays.

slides.text: On the last day of his second visit, Gandhi gave his speech to the princes studying in Rajkumar College, Raipur
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi speaking to young princes at Rajkumar College. Boys in formal dress, Gandhi in dhoti. Contrast.

slides.text: the children of kings start adopting the bad habits of the British away from the Indian language and culture, whereas in England the children of the king live like a common man
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi's words floating as text: "the children of kings start adopting the bad habits of the British..."

slides.text: Gandhi came to Chhattisgarh twice, the first time as Mohandas, the second time as a Mahatma
slides.visualDescription: Two silhouettes of Gandhi — young (1920) and older (1933) — walking toward each other, merging.

slides.text: Thousands of leaders like Pt. Ravi Shankar Shukla, Thakur Pyarelal Singh, Khubchand Baghel, Ghanshyam Singh Gupta...
slides.visualDescription: Grid of portrait silhouettes — all the leaders influenced by Gandhi, named below.

slides.text: were influenced by Gandhi's personality and engaged in the service of the country for life
slides.visualDescription: Same leaders now shown walking into light, carrying India's flag.
A charkha spinning — thread transforming into the Indian tricolor flag. Visual metaphor.

slides.text: From peasant movement to labor movement to litterateurs to artists, from students to teachers, from urban street commuters to forest dwellers
slides.visualDescription: Chhattisgarh map with flames at multiple locations — representing all the movements to come.

slides.text: The workers of Rajnandgaon fought a long battle for their rights under the leadership of Thakur Pyarelal Singh
slides.visualDescription: Women spinning charkha together, singing. Warm interior light.

slides.text: Ram Dayal Tiwari composed a book titled Gandhi Mimamsa
slides.visualDescription: Books being written — pen on paper by lamplight. "Gandhi Mimamsa" visible.

slides.text: Maulana Abdul Rauf Khan was a pioneer in the work of communal unity
slides.visualDescription: Maulana Abdul Rauf Khan and Hindu leaders standing together. Hindu-Muslim unity.

slides.text: Dr. Radhabai played the trumpet of Nari Jagran
slides.visualDescription: Dr. Radhabai leading women through streets of Raipur. Tricolor in hand.

slides.text: Shikanal Shyamlal Som and Burhan Shah did the awakening of the awakening among the forest dwellers
slides.visualDescription: Forest scene — tribals Shikanal Shyamlal Som speaking to villagers under a giant tree.

slides.text: Gandhi was sitting in the third-class compartment, the public ran on the same side
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi on train — third class compartment — looking out window at passing Chhattisgarh landscape.

slides.text: seeing Gandhi going in the third class, the public got emotional after realizing his simplicity
slides.visualDescription: Crowd at railway platform, emotional faces watching Gandhi depart. Hands reaching.

slides.text: people became convinced that only Gandhi can lead the poor and downtrodden Indian people properly
slides.visualDescription: Quote card: "people became convinced that only Gandhi can lead the poor and downtrodden Indian people properly"
Sunrise over Chhattisgarh — new day dawning, fields turning golden.
Calendar pages flying: 1920... 1930... 1942... 1947. Fast montage of years.

slides.text: On August 15, the first Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh and Berar, P. Ravi Shankar Shukla hoisted the tricolor at Sitabardi fort
slides.visualDescription: Indian flag rising over Raipur — Aug 15, 1947. Pt. Vamanrao Lakhe hoisting.
Modern Chhattisgarh skyline dissolving into the forest/village scene from slide 4. Past and present.

slides.text: during both these visits Gandhi influenced the society and every person of Chhattisgarh
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi's walking stick planted in Chhattisgarh soil — a tree growing from it. Visual metaphor.

End card — JG logo + MF logo, "A Meer Foundation Initiative". Elegant, museum-quality.
